Bismillah on slaughter: Hanafi, Maliki and Hanbali — if it is left out deliberately the meat is not lawful; if forgotten it is lawful (the Hanbali school has another narration). Shafi'i — saying it is a sunnah and the meat is lawful even if it is omitted.
Meat slaughtered by the People of the Scripture: the schools agree it is lawful if slaughtered in the lawful way; Whether supermarket meat qualifies is a question of how it was slaughtered; ask a scholar about your case.
Alcohol in small amounts as an ingredient (for example in flavorings), and gelatin: scholars differ; ask a scholar for your case.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Allah made the pure foods lawful and named what is forbidden, so that the believer eats with knowledge.
goDeeper.evidence: The first four items are the Qur'an's own text. The hadith additions are quoted with their numbers.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Assuming all meat in a shop is halal without asking; ignoring an ingredient that is intoxicating; thinking the doubtful is the same as the forbidden.

title: Sleeping Manners
subtitle: Wudu, the sleep dua, the right side, and what the Prophet recited
steps: Make wudu as for prayer and lie on your right side. The Prophet ﷺ told al-Bara', 'Whenever you go to bed, perform ablution as you do for prayer, lie on your right side and say: Allahumma aslamtu wajhi ilayka ... ' (Bukhari 247). He said that if you die that night you will die with faith (on the religion of Islam), and to let these words be your last utterance before sleep.

The Prophet ﷺ used to say when he went to bed, 'Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya' (with Your name, O Allah, I die and I live), and on waking, 'Al-hamdu lillahil-ladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur' (all praise is for Allah who gave us life after He made us die, and to Him is the resurrection) (Bukhari 6324).

Recite the three surahs. When he went to bed he used to cup his hands, blow into them after reciting al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas, and wipe his hands over whatever parts of his body he was able to reach (Bukhari 5017).

Recite Ayat al-Kursi. Abu Hurayrah was told by one who had come at night to steal, 'Whenever you go to bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi till you finish the verse. Allah will appoint a guard for you who will stay with you and no devil will come near you till morning.' The Prophet ﷺ said, 'He told you the truth, though he is a liar' (Bukhari 2311).

Surah al-Mulk. He said a surah of thirty verses intercedes for its reader until he is forgiven: 'Blessed is He in Whose hand is the dominion' (Abu Dawud 1400, hasan per al-Albani; Tirmidhi 2891, hasan per al-Albani). Jabir said he would not sleep until he had recited Alif Lam Mim Tanzil as-Sajdah and Tabarak (Tirmidhi 3404, sahih per al-Albani; Zubair Ali Zai graded it da'if, so its grade is disputed).
The night is also for prayer. He said the most excellent prayer after the prescribed prayers is the prayer in the night (Muslim 1163). See the Tahajjud guide.
sources: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 2891 (hasan per al-Albani), 3404 (sahih per al-Albani; da'if per Zubair Ali Zai)

goDeeper.why: Sleep is a small death; the Prophet taught that the day should end, like it begins, in the remembrance of Allah.
goDeeper.evidence: Bukhari 247 and 6324 give the sleep duas; Bukhari 5017 the recitation and wiping; Bukhari 2311 Ayat al-Kursi.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Sleeping without wudu or any dhikr; treating Ayat al-Kursi as a charm without understanding it.

title: Speech — The Weight of Words
subtitle: Speaking good or staying silent, and what backbiting is
steps: The standard. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should talk what is good or keep quiet' (Bukhari 6475).
Weigh what you say. He said a servant may utter a word without thinking whether it is right or wrong, and fall into the Fire as far as the distance between the east and west (Bukhari 6477).

Backbiting. Allah says, 'Do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it' (Qur'an 49:12). The Prophet ﷺ asked, 'Do you know what backbiting is?' They said Allah and His Messenger know best. He said, 'Talking about your brother in a manner he does not like.' It was asked, what if what I say is true? He said, 'If it is in him, you have backbitten him, and if it is not, you have slandered him' (Muslim 2589).

Do not search for faults. He said, 'Do not backbite Muslims and do not search for their faults, for if anyone searches for their faults, Allah will search for his fault' (Abu Dawud 4880, hasan sahih per al-Albani; Zubair Ali Zai graded it hasan). He also said, 'Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the worst of false tales, and do not look for others' faults and do not spy' (Bukhari 6064).

When speaking of a person is allowed: the scholars allow naming a wrong when needed, such as to seek justice (see Qur'an 4:148: 'Allah does not like the public mention of evil except from one who has been wronged'), to warn a person of a harm, or to ask a scholar for a ruling. Ask a scholar for the limits in your case.
Leave arguing. He said, 'I guarantee a house in the surroundings of Paradise for a man who avoids quarrelling even if he were in the right' (Abu Dawud 4800, hasan per al-Albani).
Do not deceive. He said, 'He who deceives is not of me' (Muslim 102).
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 4800 (hasan per al-Albani), 4880 (hasan sahih per al-Albani)

goDeeper.why: The tongue is the part of the body that most easily takes the heart's place; the Prophet placed speech under accountability.
goDeeper.evidence: Each rule is a quoted verse or hadith; Muslim 2589 defines backbiting in the Prophet's own words.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Calling backbiting 'just telling the truth'; spreading what you heard without checking; arguing to win.

title: Greetings & Sneezing
subtitle: The salam, how to answer, and the etiquette of sneezing and yawning
steps: Greet those you know and those you do not. A man asked the Prophet ﷺ which part of Islam is best; he said, 'To feed the poor and greet those whom you know and those whom you do not know' (Bukhari 12).

Spread the salam. He said, 'You shall not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Should I not direct you to a thing which, if you do it, will foster love among you? Spread the salam among you' (Muslim 54).

Who greets first. He said, 'The young should greet the old, the passer-by should greet the one sitting, and the small group should greet the large group' (Bukhari 6231). Allah says, 'When you are greeted with a greeting, greet with one better than it or return it [in like manner]' (Qur'an 4:86).

Sneezing. He said, 'If any of you sneezes he should say Al-hamdu lillah, and his brother or companion should say to him Yarhamukallah. When the latter says Yarhamukallah, the former should say Yahdikumullahu wa yuslih balakum' (Bukhari 6224).
Yawning. He said Allah loves sneezing and dislikes yawning; if one of you yawns he should try his best to stop it, for Satan laughs at him (Bukhari 6226).

Shaking hands. He said, 'Two Muslims will not meet and shake hands without being forgiven before they separate' (Abu Dawud 5212, sahih per al-Albani; Zubair Ali Zai graded it da'if, so its grade is disputed).

It is one of the rights of a Muslim over another: when you meet him, greet him; when he invites you, accept; when he asks your advice, advise him; when he sneezes and praises Allah, say Yarhamukallah; when he is ill, visit him; when he dies, follow his funeral (Muslim 2162).
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 5212 (sahih per al-Albani; da'if per Zubair Ali Zai)
madhhabNote: Answering the greeting: the majority hold that returning a greeting is obligatory (a collective duty when a group is greeted). Whether it is permitted to initiate the salam to a non-Muslim, and how to return their greeting, is a separate question that scholars treat in detail; ask a scholar.

goDeeper.why: The salam makes a stranger into a person to whom you have already wished peace.
goDeeper.evidence: Muslim 54 gives the command to spread it; Bukhari 12 and 6231 give who should greet whom.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Greeting only those you know; leaving a sneeze unanswered; answering a sneeze without Alhamdulillah being said.

title: Hajj — The Fifth Pillar
subtitle: Who must go, when, the three ways of performing it, and what it requires
steps: The obligation: 'And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able to find thereto a way' (Qur'an 3:97). Ability means the means to go and return, health, a safe road, and provision for the family left behind.

Once in a lifetime: the Prophet ﷺ said Allah has made Hajj obligatory; a man asked whether it was every year; he kept silent, then said: if I said yes it would become obligatory and you would not be able to do it (Muslim 1337).

The time: 'Hajj is [during] well-known months' (Qur'an 2:197): Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah and the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. The rites themselves are on the 8th to 13th of Dhul-Hijjah. Umrah may be performed at any time of the year.
A woman: the Prophet ﷺ said a woman should not travel except with a mahram (Bukhari 1862). The schools differ on whether Hajj requires one; see the note.

The three ways: on the Farewell Pilgrimage some of the Companions entered ihram for Umrah only, some for Hajj and Umrah together, and some for Hajj only (Bukhari 1562). Tamattu': Umrah first, leave ihram, then Hajj on the 8th. Qiran: Hajj and Umrah together in one ihram. Ifrad: Hajj only. The Prophet ﷺ was told to enter ihram for Hajj and Umrah together and had sacrificial animals with him (Bukhari 1534; Muslim 1218).

The sacrifice (hady): 'whoever performs 'umrah [during the Hajj months] followed by Hajj [offers] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And whoever cannot find [or afford such an animal] - then a fast of three days during Hajj and of seven when you have returned' (Qur'an 2:196). It is owed by the one who performs tamattu' or qiran.

Before departure: settle debts and return what is owed, write a will, seek forgiveness from people you have wronged, and leave provision for the family. Take halal provision: 'the best provision is fear of Allah' (Qur'an 2:197).

The reward: the Prophet ﷺ said an accepted Hajj has no reward but Paradise (Bukhari 1773), and whoever performs Hajj and does not have relations or commit sin returns as on the day his mother bore him (Bukhari 1521).
sources: The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Pillars of Hajj: Hanafi — standing at Arafah and the tawaf of Ifadah (ihram is a condition; sa'i is wajib). Maliki and Hanbali — ihram, standing at Arafah, tawaf of Ifadah and sa'i. Shafi'i — ihram, standing at Arafah, tawaf, sa'i, shaving or shortening, and the order of the rites.
The best of the three ways: Hanafi — qiran. Maliki and Shafi'i — ifrad. Hanbali — tamattu'.
A woman and a mahram: Hanafi and Hanbali — a mahram (or her husband) is required for the journey. Maliki and Shafi'i — a group of trustworthy women, or a safe road, is enough.
Umrah: Shafi'i and Hanbali — obligatory once. Hanafi and Maliki — a confirmed sunnah.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Hajj gathers the Muslims of the world at the House in the footsteps of Ibrahim.
goDeeper.evidence: Every rite below has its own guide; this one covers who must go and how.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Delaying Hajj without a reason; travelling without settling debts; not knowing which way (tamattu', qiran, ifrad) the group is performing.

title: Ihram — Entering the Sacred State
subtitle: The cloths, the intention, the talbiyah
steps: Prepare: bathe, trim, and perfume the body before the intention. Aisha said she used to perfume the Prophet ﷺ when he wanted to enter ihram (Bukhari 1539).

Men wear two unsewn cloths, an izar and a rida. The Prophet ﷺ said the muhrim does not wear a shirt, a turban, trousers, a hooded cloak, or anything scented with saffron or wars; if he has no sandals he may wear leather socks cut below the ankles (Bukhari 134, 1838). Women wear ordinary modest clothing and uncover the face and hands in ihram (Bukhari 1838).

Pray, then state the intention at the miqat: 'Labbayka Hajjan' (or 'Umratan, or both). In the valley of al-Aqiq at Dhul-Hulayfah the Prophet ﷺ said that a messenger had come to him from his Lord that night, asking him to pray in that blessed valley and to enter ihram for Hajj and Umrah together (Bukhari 1534).

The talbiyah: 'Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, innal-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk, la sharika lak' (Bukhari 1549; Muslim 1184). Men raise their voices with it: the Prophet ﷺ said Jibril came and commanded him to tell his Companions to raise their voices with the talbiyah (Abu Dawud 1814, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).

Say it often: after prayers, on climbing and descending, and on meeting others. It continues until you begin the stoning of Jamrat al-Aqabah on the 10th (for Hajj), or until you begin tawaf (for Umrah).
Stay in the state of ihram until the rites are done: see the Rites and Prohibitions guide.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 1814 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai)
The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Ihram and the intention: ihram is a condition (Hanafi) or a pillar (Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali). The intention may be said aloud with the talbiyah.
The talbiyah: Hanafi — required once (wajib) to enter ihram, or its equivalent (a dhikr or driving the hady). Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali — a sunnah.
Face covering for women: the four schools hold that a woman does not wear a niqab in ihram but may let her cloth hang down over her face if men are near; gloves are not worn.
Crossing the miqat without ihram: Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali — return to the miqat or pay a sacrifice (dam).
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Ihram strips away rank: every pilgrim stands before Allah in the same cloth.
goDeeper.evidence: The garments and the talbiyah are from Bukhari and Muslim.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Perfuming the cloths after the intention; wearing sewn garments; forgetting to say the talbiyah.

title: Tawaf & Sa'i
subtitle: Seven circuits and seven lengths — the rites Hajar taught us
steps: Enter al-Masjid al-Haram with the right foot and the entering du'a (see the Mosque guide). Approach the Black Stone: kiss it if you can (Umar said he kissed it only because he had seen the Prophet ﷺ do so: Bukhari 1597), or point to it, as the Prophet ﷺ pointed to the Corner from his mount (Bukhari 1612).

Tawaf: seven circuits beginning and ending at the Stone, the Ka'bah on your left. Men walk briskly (ramal) in the first three circuits of the arrival tawaf and walk normally in the last four (Bukhari 1602; Muslim 1218).

Between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone the Prophet ﷺ used to say: 'Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire' (Qur'an 2:201), in the report Abu Dawud 1892, hasan per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai.
After the tawaf pray two rak'ahs behind the Station of Ibrahim (Qur'an 2:125). The Prophet ﷺ recited Surah al-Ikhlas and Surah al-Kafirun in them (Muslim 1218).

Sa'i: go out to Safa. The Prophet ﷺ recited 'Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah' (Qur'an 2:158), saying he began with what Allah began with. He climbed Safa until he saw the House, faced it and said the takbir, tahlil and praise (Muslim 1218).

Walk to Marwah (one length), then back (two), seven lengths in all, ending at Marwah. Men run between the two green markers (Muslim 1218). This recalls Hajar's search for water for Ismail (Bukhari 3364).

Completion of Umrah: men shave the head or shorten the hair. The Prophet ﷺ made dua three times for those who shave and the third time for those who shorten (Bukhari 1727). For women shaving is not required, only clipping (Abu Dawud 1984, sahih per al-Albani; Zubair Ali Zai: hasan).
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 1892 (hasan per al-Albani), 1984 (sahih per al-Albani)
The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Wudu for tawaf: Hanafi — wajib; Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali — a condition (Maliki and Shafi'i and the relied-upon Hanbali view). A woman in menstruation does not perform tawaf (Bukhari 294 in the Menstruation guide).
Number of circuits: seven in the four schools. If four are done, the Hanafi school counts the tawaf as done and a sacrifice completes the rest; the others require all seven.
Sa'i: Hanafi — wajib (a sacrifice if left). Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali — a pillar of Hajj and Umrah.
The two rak'ahs after tawaf: Hanafi — wajib. Others — a sunnah.
Shaving or shortening: Hanafi, Maliki, Hanbali — wajib. Shafi'i — a pillar.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Tawaf circles the House of Allah; sa'i walks again the walk of a mother who trusted Him.
goDeeper.evidence: Each rite above carries its own source; the Jabir hadith (Muslim 1218) is the main account of the Prophet's own Hajj.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Starting the tawaf before the Stone's line; shortening the sa'i; forgetting the two rak'ahs; pushing through the crowd.

title: The Day of Arafah
subtitle: The day the religion was perfected
steps: Stand at Arafah: the Prophet ﷺ ordered a caller to proclaim that the Hajj is Arafah and that whoever reaches Jam' (Muzdalifah) at night before Fajr has caught the Hajj (Tirmidhi 889, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).
The Prophet ﷺ stayed at Arafah until the sun set and the yellow light faded, then left for Muzdalifah (Muslim 1218). Departure after sunset is the sunnah.
The best of the day: 'There is no day on which Allah frees more servants from the Fire than the Day of Arafah' (Muslim 1348).
The verse: 'This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion' (Qur'an 5:3).
The sunnah of a pilgrim is not to fast on this day. Umm al-Fadl sent a bowl of milk to the Prophet ﷺ on his camel on the day of Arafah and he drank it while people watched (Bukhari 1661).

A dua often mentioned for this day, 'La ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lah...' as 'the best of dua', is reported in Tirmidhi 3585, whose grade is disputed (Zubair Ali Zai: da'if); because it is disputed, say it as a dhikr and do not present it as a settled hadith. Make your own dua too.
sources: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 889 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai), 3585 (hasan per al-Albani; da'if per Zubair Ali Zai)
The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
The time of the standing: see the Hajj walkthrough guide for the schools' differences.
Fasting for the pilgrim: Hanafi and Maliki — not recommended; Shafi'i and Hanbali — recommended not to fast (so that he is strong for dua).
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Arafah is the heart of Hajj: no rite can be completed without it.
goDeeper.evidence: The Tirmidhi report in the sources and Muslim 1218 give the standing and its time.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Leaving before sunset; resting in the shade of the borders outside Arafah; wasting the hours in conversation.

title: Fasting — The Fourth Pillar
subtitle: From dawn to sunset, and what breaks the fast: who is excused and what is owed
steps: The command: 'O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous' (Qur'an 2:183). The month begins with sighting the crescent: the Prophet ﷺ said start fasting on seeing the crescent of Ramadan and stop on seeing the crescent of Shawwal, and if the sky is overcast complete thirty days of Sha'ban (Bukhari 1909).

The hours: 'And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the sunset' (Qur'an 2:187). Eating, drinking and sexual relations are forbidden during these hours.

The intention: the Prophet ﷺ said whoever does not resolve to fast before dawn has no fast (Abu Dawud 2454, sahih per al-Albani; Zubair Ali Zai graded it da'if). The schools differ on when and how often it is made; see the note.

Suhoor: 'Take suhoor, for in the suhoor there is blessing' (Bukhari 1923). Break the fast promptly: the people will remain on the right path as long as they hasten the breaking of the fast (Bukhari 1957). The Prophet ﷺ broke his fast with fresh dates, or dry dates, or a few mouthfuls of water (Abu Dawud 2356, hasan sahih per al-Albani; isnad hasan per Zubair Ali Zai).

Forgetfulness: whoever eats or drinks forgetfully should complete his fast, for Allah fed him and gave him drink (Bukhari 1933). Vomiting without intending to does not break it, and the one who vomits on purpose must make up the day (Abu Dawud 2380, da'if per Zubair Ali Zai; sahih per al-Albani).

The excused: 'So whoever among you is ill or on a journey [during them] — then an equal number of days [are to be made up]' (Qur'an 2:184). Hamzah ibn Amr asked the Prophet ﷺ about fasting on a journey; he said, fast if you like and break if you like (Muslim 1121).

The elderly and those unable to fast: Ibn Abbas said the verse 'upon those who are able [to fast, but with hardship] — a ransom of feeding a poor person' is not abrogated; it is for the old man and old woman who cannot fast, who feed one poor person for each day (Bukhari 4505).

A pregnant or nursing woman: the Prophet ﷺ said Allah has remitted half the prayer to the traveller, and fasting to the traveller, the nursing woman and the pregnant woman (the narrator is unsure whether he named both women or one of them) (Abu Dawud 2408, hasan sahih per al-Albani; hasan per Zubair Ali Zai). The schools differ on whether she makes up the days, feeds the poor, or both; see the note.

Deliberate intercourse in Ramadan: a man came and said 'I am ruined'; the Prophet ﷺ asked if he could free a slave, and if not, fast two months in succession, and if not, feed sixty poor people (Bukhari 1936; Muslim 1111). This is the kaffarah, in addition to making up the day.
Menstruating women do not fast and make up the days (see the Menstruation guide).
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 2356 (hasan sahih per al-Albani), 2380 (sahih per al-Albani), 2408 (hasan sahih per al-Albani), 2454 (sahih per al-Albani)
The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
The intention: Hanafi — required but may be made until before midday for the Ramadan fast. Maliki — one intention at the start of Ramadan covers the month (a nightly intention is better). Shafi'i and Hanbali — required each night before dawn for an obligatory fast.
Eating or drinking forgetfully: Hanafi, Shafi'i, Hanbali — does not break the fast. Maliki — the fast is broken and the day is made up (no kaffarah).
Kaffarah: Hanafi and Maliki — for deliberate eating, drinking or intercourse. Shafi'i and Hanbali — for intercourse only. Order: Hanafi, Shafi'i, Hanbali — freeing a slave, then fasting two months, then feeding sixty. Maliki — a choice; feeding is preferred.
Pregnant or nursing woman who fears for herself: she makes up the days; no fidyah. Who fears for the child: Hanafi — makes up the days only. Maliki — a nursing mother makes up the days and feeds a poor person for each; a pregnant woman only makes up. Shafi'i and Hanbali — makes up the days and feeds a poor person for each. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar held fidyah alone, without making up.
The elderly who cannot fast: Hanafi, Shafi'i, Hanbali — fidyah for each day. Maliki — nothing is required; fidyah is recommended.
A traveller: all four schools permit breaking the fast. Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i — fasting is better if there is no hardship. Hanbali — breaking is better.
Eye drops, injections that do not nourish: the majority hold that they do not break the fast; scholars differ on some, ask for your case.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Fasting trains the believer to obey Allah even in what is permitted, so that obedience in what is forbidden is easier.
goDeeper.evidence: Each ruling above has its own source; the differences between the schools are in the note.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Making the intention only after dawn without knowing the school's rule; breaking the fast out of fear of a small thing that does not break it; forgetting to make up days; not knowing that kaffarah is owed for deliberate intercourse.

title: Ramadan Nights
subtitle: Taraweeh, the Qur'an in Ramadan, i'tikaf and Laylat al-Qadr
steps: The reward: the Prophet ﷺ said whoever stands in prayer in the nights of Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his past sins are forgiven (Bukhari 37).

The prayer in congregation: the Prophet ﷺ prayed in the mosque, and people prayed behind him; the next night more came; on the third or fourth night he did not come out and said he had feared it would be made obligatory (Bukhari 1129).
Umar later gathered the people behind one imam, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, in the mosque and said, an excellent innovation this is (Bukhari 2010).
How many rak'ahs: Aisha said the Prophet ﷺ did not exceed eleven rak'ahs in Ramadan or outside it (Bukhari 1147). The schools differ; twenty is the practice of most congregations. See the note.

The Qur'an: Jibril met the Prophet ﷺ every night of Ramadan and they reviewed the Qur'an; he was at his most generous then (Bukhari 6). Many mosques complete the Qur'an in the taraweeh; recite at a pace you can understand.

The last ten nights: Aisha said that when the last ten began the Prophet ﷺ stayed awake at night, woke his family and tightened his waist-wrapper (Muslim 1174). He did i'tikaf in the last ten days until he died (Bukhari 2026).

Laylat al-Qadr: 'The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months' (Qur'an 97:3). Seek it in the odd nights of the last ten (Bukhari 2017). Aisha asked what to say if she found it; he told her to say 'Allahumma innaka afuwwun tuhibbul-afwa fa'fu anni' (O Allah, You are Pardoning, You love to pardon, so pardon me) (Tirmidhi 3513, sahih per al-Albani; Zubair Ali Zai graded it da'if).
sources: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3513 (sahih per al-Albani; da'if per Zubair Ali Zai)
The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Number of rak'ahs: Hanafi, Shafi'i and Hanbali — twenty (two by two), plus witr. Maliki — thirty-six in Madinah's practice, though twenty is also accepted and eleven is permitted. All four accept eleven as the Prophet's practice.
Ruling: Hanafi, Maliki, Hanbali, Shafi'i — a confirmed sunnah for men and women.
Congregation: Hanafi — the sunnah is in congregation as a collective duty on the mosque; Shafi'i — congregation is better; Hanbali — congregation is better; Maliki — praying at home is better for the one who can maintain it.
I'tikaf: Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali — a sunnah in the last ten days; the Hanafi, Shafi'i and Hanbali schools allow it for a day or less, the Maliki school requires at least a day and a night. A woman may do it in the mosque with her husband's permission.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: The nights of Ramadan are for standing before Allah; the last ten are the best of them.
goDeeper.evidence: Bukhari 37 gives the reward; Bukhari 1147 the Prophet's own number.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Arguing about eight or twenty rak'ahs; rushing the recitation; seeking Laylat al-Qadr on a single night only.

title: Istikhara — The Guidance Prayer
subtitle: Two rak'ahs and the dua of surrender
steps: What it is: the prayer of seeking Allah's choice. Jabir said the Prophet ﷺ taught them istikhara for every matter just as he taught them a surah of the Qur'an (Bukhari 6382).
How: when one of you intends to do something, he should pray two rak'ahs other than the obligatory prayer, and then say the dua (Bukhari 6382).

The dua, in meaning: O Allah, I ask You to choose for me by Your knowledge and I ask You for ability by Your power, and I ask You of Your great bounty; for You are able and I am not able, and You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen. O Allah, if You know that this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood and the end of my affair, then decree it for me; and if You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood and the end of my affair, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, and decree for me the good wherever it may be, then make me content with it. Then he mentions his need (Bukhari 6382).
Say the dua, then name the matter. You do not need a dream or a sign.

Then act: after the istikhara you consult and decide, and rely on Allah. Allah says: 'consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah' (Qur'an 3:159). If the matter becomes easy, proceed; if you find it blocked, take that as Allah's choice.
For what: for permissible matters where you must choose (a job, a marriage proposal, a move). It is not for what is obligatory or forbidden.
sources: The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
When to say the dua: before or after the salam of the two rak'ahs — the schools accept either; Hanafi and Shafi'i scholars mention saying it after the salam.
What to recite in the rak'ahs: no surah is fixed in the hadith; some scholars mention Surah al-Kafirun and al-Ikhlas.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Istikhara admits that outcomes belong to Allah: you ask to be steered and then you walk with tawakkul.
goDeeper.evidence: Bukhari 6382 contains the whole istikhara; the verse for consultation is Qur'an 3:159.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Waiting for a dream; using istikhara instead of asking knowledgeable people; making the dua without thinking of the matter.

title: Tawba — The Return
subtitle: The conditions of repentance and the door that stays open
steps: The command: 'O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance' (Qur'an 66:8). And: 'Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins' (Qur'an 39:53).
The conditions the scholars derive: (1) stop the sin now; (2) regret it; (3) resolve not to return; (4) if it wronged another person, give back what you owe or ask their forgiveness.

The door stays open: the Prophet ﷺ said Allah accepts the repentance of a servant as long as his soul does not reach his throat (Tirmidhi 3537, hasan per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai), and that whoever repents before the sun rises from the west, Allah turns to him (Muslim 2703).
Allah replaces: 'Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good' (Qur'an 25:70).

Allah's joy: the Prophet ﷺ said Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than a man who loses his riding animal carrying his food and water in the desert and finds it again (Bukhari 6308).

Keep returning: the Prophet ﷺ said, by the One in whose hand is my soul, if you did not sin, Allah would remove you and bring people who sin and seek forgiveness and He would forgive them (Muslim 2749). He himself sought forgiveness a hundred times a day (Muslim 2702).
Do not expose yourself or others: the Prophet ﷺ said whoever screens a Muslim, Allah will screen him on the Day of Resurrection (Bukhari 2442).
A report that the one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin (Ibn Majah 4250) is da'if per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai, so it is not given as a saying of the Prophet ﷺ here.
sources: Sunan Ibn Majah 4250 (da'if per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai)

goDeeper.why: Tawba is the return to Allah; it is always accepted from the one who returns sincerely.
goDeeper.evidence: The conditions of repentance are stated by the scholars (for example, in Imam al-Nawawi's Riyad al-Salihin); the hadith above give the promise.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Delaying repentance; confessing the sin to others without need; giving up after falling again.

title: Earning — Halal Livelihood
subtitle: Honest trade, no interest, fair wages, and leaving the doubtful
steps: The principle. Allah says, 'O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned' (Qur'an 2:267). The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah is good and accepts only what is good, and mentioned the man who travels far, dishevelled and dusty, raising his hands to the sky, while his food, drink and clothing are unlawful: how can his dua be answered (Muslim 1015)?
Interest. Jabir said the Prophet ﷺ cursed the one who takes interest, the one who pays it, the one who records it and the two witnesses to it, and said they are all equal (Muslim 1598).
Honest weights. 'Woe to those who give less [than due], Who, when they take a measure from people, take in full. But if they give by measure or by weight to them, they cause loss' (Qur'an 83:1-3).

Truth in the sale. He said the seller and the buyer have the option as long as they have not parted, and if both speak the truth and describe the defects and qualities, they are blessed in their transaction; if they lie and conceal, the blessing is wiped out (Bukhari 2079).
Swearing in sales. He said, 'The swearing by the seller may persuade the buyer to purchase, but it deprives the sale of Allah's blessing' (Bukhari 2087).
Pay the worker. He said, 'Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries' (Ibn Majah 2443, sahih per al-Albani).

Leave the doubtful. He said, 'Leave what makes you in doubt for what does not make you in doubt' (Tirmidhi 2518, sahih per al-Albani). And in the hadith of an-Nu'man ibn Bashir, whoever avoids doubtful matters has protected his religion and his honor (Bukhari 52).

goDeeper.why: Livelihood is a trust; what you earn is judged by how it was earned as well as how it is spent.
goDeeper.evidence: Muslim 1015 ties the acceptance of dua to lawful earnings; Muslim 1598 and Qur'an 83 give the prohibitions.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Treating a small interest as insignificant; taking a salary without doing the work; hiding a defect in a sale.

title: Marriage — The Nikah
subtitle: Consent, the guardian, witnesses, the mahr and the walimah
steps: Encouraged. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'O young people, whoever among you can marry, should marry, because it helps him lower his gaze and guard his modesty, and whoever cannot should fast, for fasting diminishes his desire' (Bukhari 5066). Allah says, 'And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male slaves and female slaves' (Qur'an 24:32).

Consent. He said, 'A matron should not be given in marriage except after consulting her, and a virgin should not be given in marriage except after her permission.' They asked, how do we know her permission? He said, 'Her silence' (Bukhari 5136; Bukhari 6946, from Aisha). A virgin who said her father had married her against her will was given the choice by the Prophet (Abu Dawud 2096, sahih per al-Albani).

The guardian. He said, 'There is no marriage except with a guardian' (Tirmidhi 1101, sahih per al-Albani; Abu Dawud 2085, sahih per al-Albani; Ibn Majah 1881, sahih per al-Albani). The schools differ on how this applies to an adult woman; see the note.

The mahr is the bride's right: 'And give the women [upon marriage] their [bridal] gifts graciously' (Qur'an 4:4). Even something small may be a mahr: the Prophet told a man to look for something, 'even an iron ring' (Bukhari 5087, the story of the woman who offered herself).
Announce it and hold a walimah. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf married, giving gold equal to the weight of a date stone, and the Prophet said to him, 'Give a banquet, even if with one sheep' (Bukhari 5167).
Treat the spouse well. He said, 'The best of you is the best to his wives, and I am the best of you to my wives' (Tirmidhi 3895, sahih per al-Albani; Zubair Ali Zai graded it hasan).
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 2085 (sahih per al-Albani), 2096 (sahih per al-Albani)
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 1101 (sahih per al-Albani), 3895 (sahih per al-Albani)
The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
The guardian: Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali — the contract is not valid without a guardian (wali); a woman may not marry herself. Hanafi — an adult sane woman may contract her own marriage, though the guardian may object if the husband is not her equal (kafa'ah) or the mahr is too low.
Witnesses: Hanafi, Shafi'i, Hanbali — two witnesses at the contract. Maliki — public announcement is required; witnesses are required at the latest before consummation.
Minimum mahr: Hanafi — ten dirhams. Maliki — a quarter dinar or three dirhams. Shafi'i and Hanbali — no minimum.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Marriage is a contract of mercy and responsibility whose conditions protect both spouses.
goDeeper.evidence: Consent, the guardian and the mahr each rest on the quoted text; the schools' details are in the note.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Marrying without the bride's real consent; treating the mahr as a price; extravagance in the walimah.

title: Illness & Patience
subtitle: Expiation, the dua over the sick, seeking treatment and visiting
steps: Illness expiates. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'No fatigue, nor disease, nor sorrow, nor sadness, nor hurt, nor distress befalls a Muslim, even if it were the prick he receives from a thorn, but that Allah expiates some of his sins for that' (Bukhari 5641).

Be patient and thankful. He said, 'Strange are the ways of a believer, for there is good in every affair of his. If he has an occasion to feel delight, he thanks Allah and that is good for him; and if he is hit by trouble he shows patience and that is good for him' (Muslim 2999).
Seek treatment. He said, 'There is no disease that Allah has created, except that He also has created its treatment' (Bukhari 5678).

The dua over the sick. Aisha said that when he visited a patient he used to say, 'Take away the disease, O Lord of the people! Cure him, for You are the One who cures. There is no cure but Yours, a cure that leaves no disease' (Bukhari 5675).
Visit the sick. He said the rights of a Muslim over another include: when he is ill, visit him (Muslim 2162).

goDeeper.why: Illness is a means by which the sins of a believer are removed and by which he turns to Allah.
goDeeper.evidence: Each item quotes the hadith; the wording of the dua is that of Bukhari 5675.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Complaining against Allah instead of to Him; refusing treatment; visiting and staying too long.

title: Gratitude — Shukr
subtitle: Thanking Allah and thanking people
steps: The promise. 'And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed, "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe"' (Qur'an 14:7).
Remember and thank. 'So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me' (Qur'an 2:152). 'And whoever is grateful is grateful for [the benefit of] himself' (Qur'an 31:12).

Gratitude in ease and hardship. The Prophet ﷺ said the believer's affair is all good: if he has an occasion to feel delight, he thanks Allah and it is good for him, and if trouble hits him he is patient and it is good for him (Muslim 2999).
Thank people too. He said, 'He who does not thank the people is not thankful to Allah' (Abu Dawud 4811, sahih per al-Albani).
The patient. 'Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account' (Qur'an 39:10).
Thank with the tongue after food and drink: 'Allah is pleased with His servant who says Al-hamdu lillah when he takes a morsel of food and when he drinks' (Muslim 2734).

goDeeper.why: Gratitude is recognising that every good thing comes from Allah, and using it as He likes.
goDeeper.evidence: Qur'an 14:7 states the promise; Muslim 2999 shows both ease and hardship.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Thanking only in words; forgetting to thank the people who helped; thinking gratitude is only for large gifts.

title: Travel — The Wayfarer's Adab
subtitle: The travel dua, company, and hurrying home
steps: The dua of departure. Ibn Umar said that when the Prophet ﷺ mounted his camel to set out on a journey, he said Allahu Akbar three times and then: 'Glory to Him Who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it, and to our Lord we shall return. O Allah, we ask You on this journey of ours for righteousness and piety, and for deeds that please You. O Allah, make this journey easy for us and shorten its distance. O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Guardian of the family. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, from a gloomy sight and from an evil return in property and family' (Muslim 1342).

On return he added: 'We return, repentant, worshipping, and praising our Lord' (Muslim 1342). Ali used to say Bismillah, then Alhamdulillah on mounting, then the verse 'Glory to Him who has subjected this to us' (Tirmidhi 3446, sahih per al-Albani; Abu Dawud 2602, sahih per al-Albani).

Appoint a leader. He said, 'When three are on a journey, they should appoint one of them as their leader' (Abu Dawud 2608, hasan sahih per al-Albani; Zubair Ali Zai graded it da'if, so its grade is disputed).
Set out early. He said, 'O Allah, bless my people in their early mornings' (Abu Dawud 2606, sahih per al-Albani).

Do not delay your return. He said, 'Travel is a kind of torment, as it prevents one from eating, drinking and sleeping properly. So when one has finished his business, he should return quickly to his family' (Bukhari 1804).
Prayer on a journey: see the Prayer While Travelling guide for shortening and combining prayers. Fasting while travelling: see the Fasting guide.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 2602 (sahih per al-Albani), 2606 (sahih per al-Albani), 2608 (hasan sahih per al-Albani; da'if per Zubair Ali Zai)
madhhabNote: The distance and duration at which a traveller may shorten the prayer differ by school; they are in the Prayer While Travelling guide.

goDeeper.why: Travel is a time when a person is dependent on Allah, and the Prophet taught words for it.
goDeeper.evidence: Muslim 1342 gives the full dua of departure and the words on return.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Leaving without the dua; neglecting prayer because of the journey; delaying the return without need.

title: The Morning & Evening Adhkar
subtitle: What the Prophet taught for the start and end of the day
steps: When: the morning adhkar are said after Fajr or at the start of the day, the evening adhkar from the afternoon until night; the hadith below give the words, and scholars give these times.

The evening dua. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said that when evening came the Prophet ﷺ used to say, 'We have entered the evening and the whole kingdom of Allah has entered the evening, and praise is due to Allah. There is no god but Allah, the One Who has no partner' and then, 'His is the sovereignty and praise is due to Him, and He is potent over everything' (Muslim 2723). In the morning the words are changed to 'we have entered the morning'.

Sayyid al-istighfar. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'The most superior way of asking for forgiveness is: Allahumma anta Rabbi la ilaha illa anta, khalaqtani wa ana abduka, wa ana ala ahdika wa wa'dika mastata'tu, a'udhu bika min sharri ma sana'tu, abu'u laka bi-ni'matika alayya, wa abu'u laka bi-dhanbi faghfir li fa innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa anta. Whoever says it during the day with firm faith and dies that day before the evening is of the people of Paradise, and likewise at night' (Bukhari 6306).

The three surahs. He said of Qul huwa Allahu ahad and the two mu'awwidhat, 'Recite them three times in the morning and the evening; they will suffice you against everything' (Abu Dawud 5082, hasan per al-Albani).

Tasbih. He said, 'Whoever says Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi one hundred times a day will be forgiven all his sins even if they were as much as the foam of the sea' (Bukhari 6405). In another narration, one hundred times in the morning and in the evening (Muslim 2692).

After each prayer. The poor among the Companions came and said the rich get the higher ranks. He said, say Subhan Allah, Alhamdulillah and Allahu Akbar thirty-three times after every prayer (Bukhari 843; Muslim 595).

goDeeper.why: The adhkar keep the day framed by the remembrance of Allah, in the words the Prophet himself used.
goDeeper.evidence: Muslim 2723 and Bukhari 6306 give two of the main morning and evening duas; Abu Dawud 5082 (hasan per al-Albani) gives the three surahs.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Reading only for the count; saying the words without understanding; omitting them when busy.

title: The New Baby — Welcome Rites
subtitle: Tahnik, the name, the aqiqah on the seventh day
steps: Tahnik. Abu Musa said a son was born to him and he took him to the Prophet ﷺ, who named him Ibrahim, did tahnik for him with a date and invoked Allah's blessing for him (Bukhari 5467). Asma' said that he asked for a date, chewed it and put his saliva in the mouth of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (Bukhari 5469).

The name. The names dearest to Allah are Abdullah and Abd al-Rahman (Muslim 2132). The Prophet ﷺ said, 'A boy is in pledge for his aqiqah. Sacrifice is made for him on the seventh day, his head is shaved and he is named' (Abu Dawud 2838, sahih per al-Albani).

The aqiqah. Aisha said the Prophet ﷺ ordered that for a boy two sheep are sufficient and for a girl one (Tirmidhi 1513, sahih per al-Albani; Zubair Ali Zai: isnad hasan). Salman ibn Amir heard him say, 'The aqiqah is to be offered for a newly born boy, so slaughter an animal for him and relieve him of his suffering' (Bukhari 5472).

The adhan in the ear. Abu Rafi' said he saw the Prophet ﷺ call the adhan in the ear of al-Hasan ibn Ali when Fatimah gave birth to him (Abu Dawud 5105, hasan per al-Albani; Zubair Ali Zai graded it da'if, so its grade is disputed). Many do it; others consider the report weak.
Pray for the child and congratulate the parents in your own words; no fixed formula is quoted here.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 2838 (sahih per al-Albani), 5105 (hasan per al-Albani; da'if per Zubair Ali Zai)
The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
The aqiqah: Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali — a confirmed sunnah. Hanafi — permissible, not a sunnah.
How many animals: Shafi'i and Hanbali — two for a boy, one for a girl. Maliki — one sheep for either.
Timing: the seventh day is preferred in all schools; if missed, the Maliki school says it lapses, while the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools permit later.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: The first days of a child are marked with the name, the tahnik and the sacrifice, which are simple acts.
goDeeper.evidence: Each rite has its own hadith, quoted with its number.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Believing the aqiqah is obligatory when the school treats it as a sunnah; extravagance; delaying the name.

title: The Rights of Parents
subtitle: Good treatment, the mother first, and after they pass
steps: The command. 'And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age [while] with you, say not to them [so much as], "uff," and do not repel them but speak to them a noble word' (Qur'an 17:23).
'And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small"' (Qur'an 17:24).

The mother first. A man asked the Prophet ﷺ who is most entitled to my good companionship. He said, 'Your mother.' The man said, then who? He said, 'Your mother.' Then who? 'Your mother.' Then who? 'Your father' (Bukhari 5971).

A serious matter. He said, 'Allah has forbidden you to be undutiful to your mothers' (Bukhari 5975). And, 'Let him be humbled into dust who sees either of his parents in old age, or both, and does not enter Paradise' (Muslim 2551).

Serving them can come before volunteering for jihad: a man asked permission to go to jihad; the Prophet ﷺ asked, 'Are your parents alive?' He said yes. He said, 'Then exert yourself in their service' (Bukhari 3004).

After their death. He said, when a man dies his deeds come to an end except three: recurring charity, knowledge from which people benefit, or a pious son who prays for him (Muslim 1631). A man said his mother died suddenly; would she have a reward if he gave charity for her? He said yes (Muslim 1004). The finest act of goodness is to treat kindly the loved ones of your father (Muslim 2552).
The limit. 'Obedience is required only in what is good' (Bukhari 7257). Parents are obeyed in what is lawful; there is no obedience to anyone in disobedience of Allah.

goDeeper.why: After the worship of Allah, the Qur'an places kindness to parents; the Prophet emphasised the mother.
goDeeper.evidence: Bukhari 5971 gives the order of the mother and father; Muslim 1631 what continues after death.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Speaking harshly in their old age; neglecting a parent because of work; forgetting their dua and charity after they die.

title: The Rights of Neighbors
subtitle: Not harming, sharing and honoring
steps: The measure. The Prophet ﷺ said three times, 'By Allah, he does not believe!' It was said, who? He said, 'The one whose neighbor does not feel safe from his evil' (Bukhari 6016). And, 'He will not enter Paradise whose neighbor is not secure from his wrongful conduct' (Muslim 46).
The Qur'an. 'Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the neighbor farther away' (Qur'an 4:36).
How much it matters. He said, 'Jibril continued to recommend me about treating the neighbors kindly and politely so much so that I thought he would order me to make them as my heirs' (Bukhari 6014).
Share food. He said to Abu Dharr, 'When you prepare broth, add water to it and give some to your neighbor' (Muslim 2625).
Which neighbor first. Aisha asked, 'I have two neighbors; to which shall I send my gifts?' He said, 'To the one whose gate is nearer to you' (Bukhari 6020).
Believing in Allah and the Last Day is tied to not harming the neighbor and to honoring the guest (Bukhari 6018).

goDeeper.why: The neighbor's right is mentioned in the same verse as worship of Allah and kindness to parents.
goDeeper.evidence: Bukhari 6016 and Muslim 46 give the severity; Muslim 2625 the practice of sharing.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Noise and rubbish; ignoring a neighbor's need; reporting a neighbor's faults.

title: Oaths & Vows
subtitle: Swearing by Allah, the kaffarah and the vow
steps: Swear only by Allah. Ibn Umar heard a man say 'No, by the Ka'bah', and said, 'I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: whoever swears by other than Allah has committed disbelief or shirk' (Tirmidhi 1535, sahih per al-Albani).
Do not swear too much. He said of the seller, 'The swearing may persuade the buyer to purchase, but it deprives the sale of Allah's blessing' (Bukhari 2087).

An oath that is meaningless is not held against you; a sworn oath that is broken needs expiation: 'Allah will not impose blame upon you for what is meaningless in your oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for [breaking] what you intended of oaths' (Qur'an 5:89).

The expiation: 'feeding of ten needy people from the average of that which you feed your [own] families or clothing them or the freeing of a slave. But whoever cannot find [or afford it] - then a fast of three days [is required]. That is the expiation for oaths when you have sworn. But guard your oaths' (Qur'an 5:89). Fasting is only for the one who cannot afford the other three.
A vow does not change anything. Ibn Umar said the Prophet ﷺ forbade vowing and said, 'Vowing does not prevent anything, but it makes a miser spend his property' (Bukhari 6608).

A vow of obedience must be kept, and a vow of disobedience must not be: 'Whoever vows that he will be obedient to Allah should obey Him; and whoever vows that he will disobey Allah should not disobey Him' (Bukhari 6696). If a vow is not fulfilled, 'The expiation for a vow is the same as for an oath' (Muslim 1645).
sources: The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Expiation: all four schools follow Qur'an 5:89. Timing: Hanafi — only after the oath is broken; Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali — it may also be paid before. The amount of food for each poor person differs by school; ask a scholar of your school.
Fasting in place of feeding: only if the person cannot afford the other three. Hanafi requires the inability at the time of paying.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: An oath calls Allah as witness, so it is kept or expiated.
goDeeper.evidence: Qur'an 5:89 gives the whole rule of expiation; Bukhari 6696 and Muslim 1645 the rule of the vow.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Swearing by other than Allah out of habit; treating fasting as a free alternative; making a vow to bargain with Allah.

title: Witr & The Night Routine
subtitle: Closing the day the way it opened — with light
steps: What it is: the odd-numbered prayer that closes the night. The Prophet ﷺ said make witr your last prayer at night (Bukhari 998), and that witr is one rak'ah at the end of the prayer (Muslim 752). Whoever fears the dawn prays one rak'ah as witr (Bukhari 990). Aisha described eleven rak'ahs, ending with three (Bukhari 1147).

Its time is between Isha and Fajr. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever fears he will not wake in the last part of the night should pray witr in the first part, and whoever is sure he will wake should pray it at the end, for the prayer of the end of the night is witnessed (Muslim 755).
Do not repeat it: Talq ibn Ali reported that the Prophet ﷺ said there are no two witrs in a night (Abu Dawud 1439, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).
If you sleep through it or forget it, pray it when you remember or wake: the Prophet ﷺ said so (Abu Dawud 1431, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai; Tirmidhi 465, sahih per al-Albani).

The qunut: the Prophet ﷺ taught his grandson al-Hasan words to say in the qunut of witr, beginning: O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, and pardon me among those You have pardoned, and take me into Your care among those You have taken into Your care... (Nasa'i 1745, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai). The schools differ on when the qunut is said; see the note.
Last words of the day: the Prophet ﷺ taught that the best way of seeking forgiveness is the Sayyid al-Istighfar (Bukhari 6306).
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 1431 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai), 1439 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai)
Sunan an-Nasa'i 1745 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai)
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 465 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai)
The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Ruling: Hanafi — witr is wajib (obligatory, below fard). Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali — a strongly emphasised sunnah.
Number and form: Hanafi — three rak'ahs with one salam and one sitting. Maliki — one rak'ah after a two-rak'ah shaf'. Shafi'i — from one to eleven, odd. Hanbali — from one to eleven, odd, with one or two sittings.
Qunut: Hanafi — in the third rak'ah before ruku', all year. Shafi'i — in the second half of Ramadan (and in Fajr all year), after ruku'. Hanbali — after ruku', all year (permitted before). Maliki — the qunut is not said in witr (it is said in Fajr).
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Witr ends the night prayer with an odd number; it is the closing of the day's worship.
goDeeper.evidence: Bukhari 998 and Muslim 755 give the practice; the report that forbids two witrs in a night is in the sources.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Praying witr twice in one night; missing it because of sleep and giving it up; counting witr as nothing because it is not fard.

title: Seeking Knowledge
subtitle: Intention, the path, and acting on what you learn
steps: The path. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'He who treads the path in search of knowledge, Allah would make that path easy, leading to Paradise for him' (Muslim 2699).

Watch the intention. He said, 'If anyone acquires knowledge that should be sought seeking the Face of Allah, but he acquires it only to get some worldly advantage, he will not experience the fragrance of Paradise' (Abu Dawud 3664, sahih per al-Albani). And, 'Actions are by intentions' (Bukhari 1).
The best learners. He said, 'The best among you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it' (Bukhari 5027).
The scholars. He said, 'The scholars are the heirs of the prophets' (Abu Dawud 3641, sahih per al-Albani; Shuaib al-Arna'ut and Zubair Ali Zai graded it da'if, so its grade is disputed).
What continues after death. He said, 'When a man dies, his acts come to an end except three: recurring charity, or knowledge by which people benefit, or a pious son who prays for him' (Muslim 1631).
Learn what is obligatory first: the prayer and how to purify for it. Start with the Prayer and Wudu guides.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 3641 (sahih per al-Albani; da'if per Zubair Ali Zai), 3664 (sahih per al-Albani)

goDeeper.why: Knowledge is a path whose first duty is to act on what is learned.
goDeeper.evidence: Muslim 2699 and 1631 are the primary texts; the other two are given with their disputed grades.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Learning to argue; collecting information without acting; learning from unreliable sources.

title: Hardship & Relief
subtitle: The duas the Prophet taught for distress and worry
steps: The dua of distress. Ibn Abbas said the Prophet ﷺ used to say at a time of distress: 'La ilaha illallahul-Azimul-Halim, la ilaha illallahu Rabbul-arshil-azim, la ilaha illallahu Rabbus-samawati wa Rabbul-ardi wa Rabbul-arshil-karim' (Bukhari 6346).

The dua of Yunus. He said, 'The supplication of Dhun-Nun when he supplicated in the belly of the whale was: La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin. No Muslim supplicates with it for anything except that Allah answers him' (Tirmidhi 3505, sahih per al-Albani). The verse is in Qur'an 21:87-88: 'There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.' ... 'So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.'

Worry and grief. Anas said the Prophet ﷺ used to say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge with You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from being heavily in debt and from being overpowered by men' (Bukhari 6369).

Debt. Ali taught a man who could not pay his debt: 'Allahumma-kfini bi-halalika an haramika wa aghnini bi-fadlika amman siwak' (O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and make me independent by Your favor of all others). If he had a debt like a mountain, Allah would fulfill it (Tirmidhi 3563, hasan per al-Albani).
Patience. 'Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account' (Qur'an 39:10). And the believer's affair is all good (Muslim 2999).
sources: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3505 (sahih per al-Albani), 3563 (hasan per al-Albani)

goDeeper.why: In hardship the Prophet taught turning to Allah with known words and keeping patience.
goDeeper.evidence: Each dua is quoted from its hadith; the words in Arabic will be shown in the recitation cards.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Despair; asking only people; abandoning the duas when relief is slow.

title: Preparing — The Practical Will
subtitle: The will, debts, and what continues after you
steps: Write the will. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'It is not permissible for any Muslim who has something to will to stay for two nights without having his last will and testament written and kept ready with him' (Bukhari 2738).

The limit of one third. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas asked to will half his property; the Prophet ﷺ said half is too much. He asked for one third; he said, 'One-third, yet even one-third is too much' (Bukhari 2744).

No bequest to an heir. He said, 'Allah has given everyone who has a right his due, so no bequest may be made to an heir' (Abu Dawud 2870, hasan sahih per al-Albani; Tirmidhi 2120, sahih per al-Albani). The fixed shares of the heirs are set by Allah in Surah an-Nisa'.
Debts. He said all the sins of a martyr are forgiven except debt (Muslim 1886). Record what you owe and what is owed to you.
Last words. He said, 'If anyone's last words are La ilaha illallah, he will enter Paradise' (Abu Dawud 3116, sahih per al-Albani).
Funeral. He said, 'Hurry up with the dead body, for if it was righteous, you are forwarding it to welfare; and if it was otherwise, you are putting off an evil thing from your necks' (Bukhari 1315).
What continues. Recurring charity, knowledge from which people benefit, or a pious son who prays for him (Muslim 1631).
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 2870 (hasan sahih per al-Albani), 3116 (sahih per al-Albani)
The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Making a will: it is obligatory if one owes a debt or a trust that others do not know about. Otherwise, the majority of scholars hold that a will for relatives who are not heirs is recommended, since the verse (2:180) was followed by the verses of inheritance.
A bequest to an heir: the majority hold it is not valid unless the other heirs consent after his death. The limit is one third of the estate in all four schools.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: A will protects the rights of the family and settles the debts one owes.
goDeeper.evidence: Bukhari 2738 and 2744 give the will and its limit; Abu Dawud 2870 (hasan sahih per al-Albani) the rule on heirs.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Dying with undeclared debts; leaving more than a third to non-heirs; leaving no instruction for the funeral.

title: Hajj — Step-by-Step Walkthrough
subtitle: The full journey, day by day, from ihram to the farewell tawaf
steps: Enter ihram at the miqat with the intention for Hajj (and Umrah, if you are doing tamattu' or qiran). The Prophet ﷺ entered at Dhul-Hulayfah (Muslim 1218).
The 8th of Dhul-Hijjah (Tarwiyah): go to Mina in ihram. The Prophet ﷺ prayed Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha and Fajr there and stayed until the sun rose (Muslim 1218).

The 9th (Arafah): go to Arafah. The Prophet ﷺ stayed at Namirah until the sun passed the meridian, gave the sermon in the valley, then prayed Dhuhr and Asr together with one adhan and two iqamahs (Muslim 1218). Stand, face the qiblah, and make dua until sunset. 'The Hajj is Arafah' (Tirmidhi 889, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai). Do not leave before sunset (Muslim 1218).

After sunset go to Muzdalifah without praying Maghrib on the way. The Prophet ﷺ prayed Maghrib and Isha together there with one adhan and two iqamahs, slept until dawn, prayed Fajr, then stood at al-Mash'ar al-Haram making dua until it was very light, and left before sunrise (Muslim 1218). Collect pebbles.

The 10th (Nahr): stone Jamrat al-Aqabah with seven pebbles, saying Allahu akbar with each (Muslim 1218). Then the sacrifice (hady) for tamattu' and qiran. Then shave or shorten (Bukhari 1727). This is the first release: all prohibitions end except relations.
Go to Makkah for the tawaf of Ifadah and, if you have not yet done it (tamattu' and, in some schools, ifrad and qiran), the sa'i of Hajj. After it all prohibitions end.

The 11th, 12th (and 13th) — the days of Tashriq: stay at Mina and stone the three jamarat after the sun passes the meridian, seven pebbles each (Bukhari 1746). Whoever hastens may leave after two days; 'and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him' (Qur'an 2:203; Tirmidhi 889, sahih per al-Albani).

Farewell: before leaving Makkah, make the farewell tawaf as your last act. The people were ordered to make the last thing the tawaf, except the menstruating women, who were excused (Bukhari 1755; Muslim 1327).
sources: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 889 (sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai)
The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Standing at Arafah: Hanafi, Shafi'i, Hanbali (the relied-upon view) — from the sun's passing the meridian; Maliki — the pillar is standing in the night of Arafah; the day standing until sunset is wajib. Hanbali — from dawn of the 9th is valid, though the Sunnah is after the meridian.
Stay at Muzdalifah: Hanafi — wajib to stand after Fajr; Maliki — enough to stop and pray there; Shafi'i and Hanbali — a wajib (stay after midnight; the weak and women may leave after midnight).
Stoning: Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali — wajib on the 10th through the 12th (or 13th). The time on the 11th-12th: after the meridian in the four schools (Hanafi: a concession before the meridian on the 13th).
Mina nights: Hanafi — a sunnah; the other three — wajib.
Farewell tawaf: Hanafi, Shafi'i, Hanbali — wajib; Maliki — a sunnah.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Follow your group's guide (mutawwif) for times and crowds; these are the Prophet's own rites.
goDeeper.evidence: Muslim 1218 is Jabir's account of the whole Farewell Pilgrimage.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Leaving Arafah before sunset; praying Maghrib on the road; stoning before the meridian on the days of Tashriq; leaving Makkah without the farewell tawaf.

title: Umrah — In a Day
subtitle: The smaller pilgrimage, complete from ihram to release
steps: Enter ihram at the miqat: bathe, put on the two cloths, pray, and say 'Labbayka Umratan' and the talbiyah (see the Ihram guide).
Go to al-Masjid al-Haram with the talbiyah on your tongue. Stop it when you begin the tawaf.
Tawaf: seven circuits from the Black Stone, the Ka'bah on your left; men walk briskly in the first three (Bukhari 1602; Muslim 1218).
Two rak'ahs behind the Station of Ibrahim if possible (Qur'an 2:125; Bukhari 1647). Then drink Zamzam.
Sa'i: seven lengths from Safa to Marwah, men running between the green markers (Muslim 1218; Qur'an 2:158).
Release: men shave the head or shorten the hair; women clip a little from the ends (Bukhari 1727; Abu Dawud 1984, sahih per al-Albani). The Umrah is complete.
During an Umrah before the Hajj season (tamattu'), you leave ihram and wear ordinary clothes until the Hajj ihram on the 8th (Bukhari 1562).
sources: The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Ruling: Shafi'i and Hanbali — obligatory once in a lifetime. Hanafi and Maliki — a confirmed sunnah.
Pillars: Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali — ihram, tawaf and sa'i (Shafi'i adds shaving or shortening). Hanafi — tawaf (four circuits); ihram is a condition; sa'i is wajib.
Women: ramal and shaving are for men only.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Umrah is a small pilgrimage: ihram, tawaf, sa'i, release, in a few hours.
goDeeper.evidence: Bukhari 1647 describes the Prophet's tawaf, prayer and sa'i in order.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Leaving ihram before the sa'i is complete; shaving without ihram status; skipping the talbiyah.

title: Arafah — Observing the Day at Home
subtitle: The 9th of Dhul-Hijjah for the one who is not on Hajj
steps: These days are the best of the year: the Prophet ﷺ said no good deeds done on other days are better than those done in these ten days (Bukhari 969).
Fast the day of Arafah if you are not on Hajj: the Prophet ﷺ said it expiates the previous year and the coming year (Muslim 1162).
Do the opposite of what the pilgrim does: fasting is for the one who is at home (Bukhari 1661 shows that the Prophet ﷺ did not fast on Arafah during Hajj).
Remember Allah in the numbered days: 'And remember Allah during [specific] numbered days' (Qur'an 2:203). Say the takbir, tahlil and tahmid often.
Make dua: the forgiveness of this day is wide: 'There is no day on which Allah frees more servants from the Fire than the Day of Arafah' (Muslim 1348).
Eid al-Adha follows on the 10th: see the Eid guide.
sources: The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Fasting Arafah for a non-pilgrim: recommended in the four schools. The Hanafi school mentions that the fast should not make one weak for dua.
The first ten days: fasting the first nine days is recommended (a sunnah) in all schools; the fast of the tenth is forbidden.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Arafah is a day for everyone, not only pilgrims: fast, remember Allah and ask forgiveness.
goDeeper.evidence: Muslim 1162 and Bukhari 969 are the sources of the fast and the ten days.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Fasting on the 10th; skipping the dua; treating the day as an ordinary day.

title: Ihram — Rites and Prohibitions
subtitle: What the muhrim must avoid and what to pay if he fails
steps: Forbidden in ihram for men: the sewn garments listed above, covering the head. For women: face veil and gloves. For both: perfume, cutting hair or nails, hunting and killing game, a marriage contract, sexual relations (Bukhari 134, 1838; Muslim 1409; Qur'an 2:197).
Marriage: 'A muhrim must neither marry himself nor arrange the marriage of another' (Muslim 1409).
Game: 'do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram' (Qur'an 5:95).
Intimacy: 'no sexual relations and no disobedience and no disputing during Hajj' (Qur'an 2:197).

Fidyah for shaving the head from necessity: the Prophet ﷺ told Ka'b ibn Ujrah, whose lice were troubling him, to shave and then fast three days, feed six poor people, or sacrifice a sheep (Bukhari 1814; Qur'an 2:196).
A violation by mistake or forgetfulness: the schools differ on whether anything is owed; see the note.
A pilgrim who dies in ihram: wash him with water and sidr, shroud him in his two cloths, and do not perfume him or cover his head; he will be resurrected saying the talbiyah (Bukhari 1265).
sources: The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Cutting hair or nails by necessity: the fidyah in Qur'an 2:196 (three days' fast, six poor people fed, or a sheep) applies in all four schools. Cutting without necessity: Hanafi — a sheep; others — the same options.
Intercourse before the standing at Arafah: invalidates the Hajj in the four schools; the pilgrim completes it, repeats it the next year and pays a sacrifice. After the standing but before the first release: Hanafi — a camel or cow; Maliki — invalidates; Shafi'i and Hanbali — a camel or cow, the Hajj stays valid.
Perfume and covering the head: Hanafi — a sacrifice if it lasts a day or more, charity if less. Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali — the three-way fidyah.
Forgetfulness: Hanafi and Maliki — the penalty applies except in a few cases. Shafi'i and Hanbali — no sin and no fidyah for forgetfulness or ignorance in most prohibitions.
Hunting: the penalty of Qur'an 5:95 in the four schools; the Hanafi school requires the value of the animal.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: The prohibitions train the pilgrim to put restraint on what is otherwise lawful.
goDeeper.evidence: Qur'an 2:196, 2:197 and 5:95 are the foundation; the hadith above give examples.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Treating the fidyah as optional for anything; killing an insect from irritation without asking; wearing scented soap.

title: How Zakat Works — The Essentials
subtitle: The third pillar: what it is, the nisab and rate, and who receives it
steps: The command. 'And establish prayer and give zakah and bow with those who bow' (Qur'an 2:43). Allah told His Prophet: 'Take, [O, Muhammad], from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them increase' (Qur'an 9:103). When he sent Mu'adh to Yemen he told him to teach them that Allah has made zakat obligatory on their property, 'to be taken from the wealthy among them and given to the poor' (Bukhari 1395).

The nisab and the year. He said, 'There is no zakat on less than five awsuq (of food-grains), and none on less than five awaq (200 dirhams) of silver' (Bukhari 1447). For gold, the hadith of Ali mentions twenty dinars: 'When you possess two hundred dirhams and one year passes on them, five dirhams are payable. Nothing is incumbent on gold till it reaches twenty dinars; when you possess twenty dinars and one year passes on them, half a dinar is payable' (Abu Dawud 1573, sahih per al-Albani; Zubair Ali Zai graded it da'if, so its grade is disputed). In modern weights scholars give about 85 g of gold or 595 g of silver; use a current price.

The rate. Abu Bakr's letter on zakat, which he wrote down for Anas, says: 'For silver the zakat is one-fortieth (2.5%), and if its value is less than 200 dirhams, zakat is not required' (Bukhari 1454). The same rate is applied by scholars to gold, cash and trade goods.
Crops. 'On land irrigated by rain or by natural water channels, one-tenth is compulsory; on land irrigated by the well, half of a tenth (one-twentieth)' (Bukhari 1483).

The recipients. 'Zakah expenditures are only for the poor and for the needy and for those employed to collect [zakah] and for bringing hearts together [for Islam] and for freeing captives [or slaves] and for those in debt and for the cause of Allah and for the [stranded] traveler' (Qur'an 9:60). These are the eight categories; zakat is not a general donation.
Use the Zakat calculator in the app for your amount; it states which school's rules it applies.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 1573 (sahih per al-Albani; da'if per Zubair Ali Zai)
The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Women's jewelry worn for adornment: Hanafi — zakat is due. Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali — not due on lawful jewelry in ordinary use.
Crops: Hanafi — one-tenth or one-twentieth on all produce of the land, with no minimum. Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali — only on stored staple crops that reach five awsuq.
Debts and the nisab: schools differ; the Zakat calculator states the rule of the school you choose.
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: Zakat purifies the wealth and the giver, and returns a right to the community.
goDeeper.evidence: The nisab, the rate and the recipients are quoted from their texts; the schools' differences are in the note.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Paying zakat on the wrong amount; delaying it past the year; giving it to someone not in the eight categories.

title: Zakat al-Fitr — The Fast-Breaking Charity
subtitle: Who pays it, how much, when, and to whom
steps: What it is: a charity due at the end of Ramadan. Ibn Abbas said the Prophet ﷺ prescribed it as a purification for the fasting person from idle talk and obscenity, and as food for the poor (Abu Dawud 1609, hasan per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai; Ibn Majah 1827, hasan per al-Albani, isnad hasan per Zubair Ali Zai).
Who pays: every Muslim, slave or free, male or female, young or old (Bukhari 1503; Muslim 984). The head of the household pays for those he supports.

How much: one sa' of dates or one sa' of barley (Bukhari 1503). Abu Sa'id said they gave one sa' of food: barley, raisins, cottage cheese or dates (Bukhari 1510). A sa' is a measure of volume; its weight depends on the food. Bukhari's note gives about 3 kg; take the figure from your mosque or scholar.

When: before the Eid prayer. The Prophet ﷺ ordered it paid before the people went out to the prayer (Bukhari 1503, 1509). Whoever pays it before the prayer, it is an accepted zakat; whoever pays it after, it is ordinary charity (Abu Dawud 1609, hasan per al-Albani).
To whom: to the poor (Abu Dawud 1609, hasan per al-Albani). The schools differ on whether other categories of zakat recipients may receive it; see the note.
Food or money: the Prophet ﷺ fixed foods; the schools differ on whether the value may be paid instead; see the note.
sources: The differences between the schools stated in the madhhab note are the standard positions of each school; they have not yet been reviewed by a named scholar.
madhhabNote:
Cash or food: Hanafi — the value in money may be paid (and is often better for the poor). Maliki and Shafi'i — food only, from the local staple. Hanbali — food (the relied-upon view); some Hanbali scholars permit the value when there is a need.
The sa': Hanafi — about 3.8 kg (the Iraqi sa'). Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali — about 2.0-3.0 kg (the Hijazi sa', depending on the food). Use the figure announced by your local scholars.
Timing: the days at the end of Ramadan, up to the Eid prayer; the schools allow paying in advance for different periods (Hanafi: any time; Maliki and Hanbali: one or two days before; Shafi'i: from the start of Ramadan).
Who must pay: every Muslim who owns more than their food for the day and night of Eid (Hanafi: the nisab).
Follow one school's fiqh for your own practice, or ask a teacher of your school.

goDeeper.why: It closes the fast: it cleans what went wrong in Ramadan and feeds the poor for Eid.
goDeeper.evidence: Bukhari 1503 gives the measure and the deadline; the Abu Dawud report in the sources gives the purpose.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Paying after the Eid prayer and thinking it counts as zakat al-Fitr; forgetting a child or a dependent; paying cash where your school requires food.

title: Giving Beyond the Obligation
subtitle: Voluntary charity: hidden, small, and in many forms
steps: The promise. 'The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed [of grain] which grows seven spikes; in each spike is a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills' (Qur'an 2:261).

Hidden or open. 'If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you' (Qur'an 2:271).
